captions.linkedin:
Stop running vol-targeting for the Sharpe boost. The 2017 paper said yes. The 2020 paper said no. Run it for the drawdown reduction, which is the part that actually held up out of sample.

Vol-targeting is a risk overlay, not a return signal. Moreira and Muir (2017), Journal of Finance, reported in-sample Sharpe gains. Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang and Yan (2020), JFE, tested 103 strategies out of sample and found the Sharpe gain was statistically insignificant. The drawdown reduction was real.

Here's the complete logic, no black box:

🔹 VOL ESTIMATE. Rolling 20 or 60-day realized vol, or EWMA. Annualized. Use only data through t-1.
🔹 LEVERAGE SCALING. Weight equals target vol divided by realized vol. Reduce exposure in stress. Boost it in calm.
🔹 REGIME TRIM. Volatility clusters. So this trims exposure *before* the worst drawdowns, not after.
🔹 CAP AND BANDS. Cap leverage at 1.5 to 3x. Use a no-trade band of plus-or-minus 10 to 20% to keep turnover sane.
🔹 STRUCTURAL FACT. Volatility forecasts volatility better than returns forecast returns. That's the entire foundation.
🔹 HONEST SCOPE. CVaR and drawdown reduction is structural. Sharpe gain is contested and probably overstated by publication bias.

Source: Moreira and Muir (2017), Journal of Finance. Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang and Yan (2020), Journal of Financial Economics. Educational use only.

The industry sells this as alpha. The cleanest read of the literature says it's risk control. That's still worth deploying.

captions.facebook:
Stop running volatility targeting for the Sharpe boost.

Moreira and Muir published a 2017 paper in the Journal of Finance reporting Sharpe gains from vol-managed factor portfolios. Three years later, Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang and Yan tested it out of sample on 103 strategies. The Sharpe improvement was statistically insignificant.

What survived: the drawdown reduction. That's structural. Run vol-targeting as a risk overlay, not as an alpha source.

The complete logic:

🔹 Estimate realized vol from a rolling 20 or 60-day window, or EWMA. Annualize. Use only data through t-1 to avoid look-ahead bias.
🔹 Weight equals target vol divided by realized vol. Reduce exposure in stress. Boost in calm.
🔹 Because volatility clusters and mean-reverts, this trims exposure *before* the worst drawdowns rather than after.
🔹 Cap leverage at 1.5 to 3x. Use a no-trade band of plus-or-minus 10 to 20% to control turnover.
🔹 Volatility forecasts volatility much better than returns forecast returns. That's the structural foundation.
🔹 The CVaR and drawdown reduction is robust. The Sharpe gain is contested.

Source: Moreira and Muir (2017), Journal of Finance. Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang and Yan (2020), Journal of Financial Economics. Educational use only.
